subject: Dedicated capacity ramp & prepay — phased GPU/TPM commit schedule
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@acme.ai>
Cc: Tom Wallace <tom@acme.ai>
Date: 2025-11-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity proposal — phased ramp schedule (initial)

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. As promised, attached is an initial proposal for Dedicated capacity with a phased ramp schedule we think maps to Acme's Q1–Q3 rollout. High-level:

- Baseline commit (Month 1): 2x A100-equivalent GPUs (approx. 200 TPM sustained)
- Month 4: increase to 4x GPUs (~450 TPM sustained)
- Month 9: increase to 8x GPUs (~900 TPM sustained)

We modeled two billing/term approaches: annual prepay (year-by-year invoiced up front) and a 3-year prepay (single upfront payment) with graduated term discounts. Key open items we need your input on: preferred prepay term, desired discount range, and whether Acme wants a strict ramp milestone schedule (we can do milestone-based billing/true-ups).

I've attached RED-4589_Dedicated_Ramp_Proposal_v1.pdf with line-item pricing and a simple ramp diagram. If you can share any internal acceptance criteria for each phase (e.g., production traffic % or date targets) we can lock the milestones into the agreement.

Goal on our side is to provide predictable unit economics for you while protecting both parties with a sensible true-up and ramp protection.

Would love to jump on a quick call to walk through the two term/discount scenarios — I'm available this week.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachment: RED-4589_Dedicated_Ramp_Proposal_v1.pdf (PDF, 4 pages)
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@acme.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Wallace <tom@acme.ai>
Date: 2025-11-03T10:05:42-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal — phased ramp schedule (initial)

Marcus,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposal. A few clarifying questions from procurement/finance:

1) Discounting: Can you provide concrete discount ranges for annual prepay vs 3-year prepay? Our finance team is looking for a 10–15% baseline on multi-year commitments.
2) True-up mechanics: We need a clear annual true-up (one-time reconciliation at the anniversary) with explicit calculation for over/under usage. Is a quarterly true-up possible instead?
3) Ramp enforcement: We'll need milestone-based commitments (dates + GPU counts). If we miss a milestone, we need a pre-agreed grace period and a true-up cap.
4) Cancellation / early termination: What refunds or credits are available if we materially slow the ramp?

I've attached our internal preferred ramp spreadsheet (acme_moa_schedule.xlsx) — it shows a slower 9–12 month ramp. Can you respond with pricing for that variant and the faster ramp you proposed? Also please include any SLA credit language tied to Dedicated capacity.

CCing Tom from procurement to keep legal/finance in the loop.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Ops, Acme AI
elena@acme.ai

Attachment: acme_moa_schedule.xlsx (Excel, 2 sheets)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-04T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal — phased ramp schedule (pricing + options)

Elena — thanks for the spreadsheet, helped a lot. I've looped in Marissa (Sales Lead) and Dev (SE) and updated the proposal with two concrete options (see attached RED-4589_Dedicated_Ramp_Proposal_v3.pdf):

Option A — Conservative (aligns with Acme spreadsheet)
- 12-month linear ramp (start 2x GPUs -> +1 GPU every 2 months until 8 GPUs)
- Annual prepay: 7% discount (invoiced up front per year)
- 3-year prepay: 15% discount (single upfront payment)
- Annual true-up at contract anniversary; quarterly reporting available on request
- Early termination: pro-rata refund for unused prepaid months minus 20% service/transition fee

Option B — Accelerated (frontloaded)
- 6-month ramp (start 2x -> 4x at M3 -> 8x at M6)
- Annual prepay: 10% discount (due to faster resource commitment)
- 3-year prepay: 18% discount (frontload premium)
- True-up: quarterly reconciliation with smaller year-end true-up
- We can add explicit milestone acceptance criteria tied to traffic % or deployment gates

SLA credits: standard Redwood Dedicated SLA applies; for multi-GPU customers we can amend to add a 5% service credit for any month where availability < 99.5% sustained across reserved pool.

Next steps we recommend: pick Option A or B and indicate whether you'd like a 1-year vs 3-year prepay. We'll then formalize milestone dates and feed into legal for a PO + DocuSign-ready exhibit.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/RED-4589 (proposal and pricing matrix posted)

Attachment: RED-4589_Dedicated_Ramp_Proposal_v3.pdf (PDF, 6 pages)
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@acme.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-05T09:48:00-08:00
Subject: Technical appendix: mapping GPUs to TPM, burst handling, and caching notes

Elena / Marcus / Marissa — quick technical note to accompany the commercial options:

- GPU -> TPM assumptions: our pricing model uses sustained TPM equivalence. Example mapping in the appendix: 1x A100-equivalent ~ 100 sustained TPM (varies by sequence length and prompt mix). The proposal already accounts for typical seq=2048 workloads.
- Burst pool: we can provide a shared burst pool for short spikes (up to 30% above committed for up to 72 hours) billed as burst usage at a discounted overage rate.
- Prefix/KV caching: many customers see 15–30% effective token reduction for repeated prefixes; enabling caching reduces your effective cost and can be a lever to defer GPU scaling.
- True-up telemetry: we will export per-token usage, instance-hours, and average sustained TPM per GPU to the shared Drive folder for audit.

If you want, I can produce a month-by-month amortization that reconciles GPU-hours to invoiced prepay and expected TPM.

Attachment: RED-4589_Technical_Appendix.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@acme.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Wallace <tom@acme.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-07T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal — phased ramp schedule (Acme counterproposals)

Marcus / team — thanks for the clarity. Procurement and finance conferred and we are willing to commit to a 3-year prepay if Redwood can accept the following commercial anchors:

1) Discount: 18% off list for a 3-year single upfront prepay (we're proposing this in exchange for month-by-month ramp milestones; we can accept a slightly slower ramp than Option B but faster than Option A).
2) Ramp milestones: commit to 4 GPUs by month 3 and 8 GPUs by month 6. Those are non-negotiable for our roadmap.
3) True-up: annual reconciliation; if usage materially exceeds committed TPM, we will true-up at agreed overage rate capped at 25% over the prepaid amount for year 1.
4) SLA: include a 5% monthly credit for availability < 99.5% specifically for the dedicated pool.

If you can accept those anchors, we'll route to legal/finance for a final PO. We're also attaching our redline guidance and will need the quote in DocuSign format.

Please confirm by EOD Friday so we can keep our internal finance deadlines.

Thanks,
Elena

Attachment: (Acme redline guidance referenced in body)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Tom Wallace <tom@acme.ai>
Date: 2025-11-10T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal — phased ramp schedule (final commercial response)

Elena / Tom — appreciate the clear anchors. After internal calibration I have the following counteroffer which I believe is commercially equivalent and keeps your ramp intact:

- 3-year single upfront prepay discount: 17% (we can stretch to 17% but not 18% due to upfront capacity reservation risk)
- Ramp milestones: agree to 4 GPUs by month 3 and 8 GPUs by month 6 as requested; milestone-based acceptance criteria to be added to the SOW (dates + deployment %).
- True-up: annual reconciliation at contract anniversary; we will cap year-1 true-up exposure at 25% over prepaid amount as you requested.
- SLA: include 5% monthly credit for availability < 99.5% across the dedicated pool.
- Change control: material reductions to committed GPUs require 60 days' notice and are subject to a ramp-adjustment fee (to protect capacity commitments).

Next steps:
1) If this is acceptable, we'll generate a DocuSign-ready exhibit and final quote (RED-4589_Final_Quote.pdf) and route to your legal/finance.
2) We'll add the milestone schedule to the SOW and publish the technical appendix and monthly telemetry folder (Drive link).

We can also add a quarterly reporting cadence if that helps your finance team for forecasting.

Please confirm and I'll kick off the paperwork.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachment: RED-4589_Final_Quote.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)
